product: VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 - VCF Automation (VM Apps organization APIs)

provenance.statement: READ THIS FIRST. This contract is NOT a published specification and is not generated from one. VCF Automation - the VCF 9.1 successor to vRealize Automation and Aria Automation - has no OpenAPI or Swagger document in the vmware/vcf-api-specs repository (Apache-2.0), and Broadcom does not publish a downloadable specification for it. Every fact below was transcribed by hand from the human-readable xAPIs reference guides on developer.broadcom.com and is therefore only as accurate and as current as those pages were on the date recorded in derivedOn. Treat it as a transcription of reference documentation, not as an authoritative schema.
provenance.referenceChannel: The xAPIs reference is versioned by channel rather than by URL. Every source URL uses the 'latest' channel, which served VCF Automation 9.1 on the fetch date. A later channel rotation can change these pages without changing their URLs.
limitations: Only the five operations named in this contract were transcribed. Other operations exist in the same reference guides and are deliberately out of scope.

The reference guides do not publish an error-response body schema for these operations. Only status codes are documented, so a client must read the status code as the authoritative signal and treat any error body as best-effort, free-form diagnostic text.
Field-level defaults are recorded only where the reference page states them explicitly.

Because no specification exists, this contract cannot be machine-validated against the product. Divergence must be resolved by re-reading the source pages listed in docs/official_sources.json, not by editing this file to match observed behaviour.

baseUri.note: One appliance FQDN fronts every service below; the service prefix is part of the path, e.g. /project-service/api, /catalog/api, /deployment/api.

tokenSource.note: Obtained against SDDC Manager, not against VCF Automation. The shipped module acquires it through the VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager cmdlets Initialize-VcfTokenCreationSpec and Invoke-CreateToken.

omitUnsetOptionalFields.rule: A request body MUST contain a key only when the caller actually supplied a value for it. An unsupplied optional field is OMITTED from the JSON object. Sending it as null, as an empty string, as 0, or as an empty object is a contract violation.
omitUnsetOptionalFields.basis: This is a house rule of this contract, not a documented guarantee of the API. Every body field in both write operations is optional, and the reference pages do not say how the service distinguishes 'not supplied' from 'supplied as empty'. The generated VMware.Sdk.Vcf.* Initialize-* cmdlets drop unbound parameters from the body they build, so this module matches that behaviour rather than inventing a second convention. It also avoids the well-known vRealize/Aria failure mode where a null day-2 input is interpreted as a request to clear the current value.

onlyDocumentedQueryParameters.rule: A request MUST NOT carry a query parameter that this contract does not list for that operation. Where a needed filter has no documented parameter, filter client-side after retrieving the page.

jsonBodies.rule: Write operations send Content-Type: application/json. A charset parameter is permitted.

getAllProjects.responseNotes: PageOfProjects wraps a content array of Project records: id, name, description, orgId, administrators, members.
getAllProjects.callerNote: There is NO documented parameter for filtering projects by name. Retrieve the page and match on name client-side.

queryParameters.name: search
queryParameters.description: Matches items whose name or description contains this string. Substring match, not exact.

getCatalogItems.responseNotes: PageCatalogItem wraps a content array of CatalogItem records: id (uuid, required), name (required), projectIds (required), type (required), plus description, isRequestable, bulkRequestLimit, sourceId, sourceName and others.
getCatalogItems.callerNote: search is a substring match, so the exact name must still be confirmed client-side.

requestBody.fieldNote: The reference marks every field optional. That is a statement about schema validation, not about usefulness: a request with no projectId will not place the deployment in a project.

requestCatalogItemInstances.responseNotes: An ARRAY, one entry per requested deployment. Each entry carries only deploymentId and deploymentName. This is the only place the deployment identifier is returned, so it must be captured here.

getDeploymentResources.responseNotes: PageDeploymentResource wraps a content array plus empty, first, last, number, numberOfElements, size, totalElements and totalPages. Each resource carries id, name, description, type, state, createdAt, expense, currentRequest and properties.
getDeploymentResources.callerNote: names is an exact-name filter, so it is the correct way to locate a single named resource.

fields.name: actionId
fields.description: Id of the action to perform.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: Reason for requesting a day-2 operation.

responses.meaning: Request state conflict. Documented, and expected whenever the target already has a request in flight - a day-2 action cannot be submitted against a resource whose provisioning request has not finished.

submitResourceActionRequest.responseNotes: The Request object carries actionId, status, createdAt, deploymentId, resourceIds, inputs, outputs and execution tracking fields such as completedTasks, totalTasks and estimatedCompletionTime.

outOfScope.note: These operations are documented in the same reference guides but are NOT part of this contract and must not be called by the change flow.
outOfScope.rationale: A change flow that fails partway through must report what it did. It must not try to tidy up by deleting a deployment the operator has not been told about.
